ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions designations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and Canada's domestic criminal-law terrorist listing framework. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by FINTRAC require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. North American and EU anti-money-laundering watchlists and adverse-media checks are applied as market-standard benchmarks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada), including the NUANS Name Search and pre-approved federal name reservation module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or bilingual. Names using foreign scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal name must include a required legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporée, or Limitée. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing federal or provincial name, trade-mark, or trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporations Canada refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Director within 30 days of the rejection, attaching a current NUANS report and written submissions distinguishing any conflicting names, marks, or trade names. If the reconsideration is refused, judicial review may be sought in the Federal Court of Canada under section 14 of the Canada Business Corporations Act; the application for judicial review must be commenced within 30 days of the refusal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for federal registered-office purposes provided that a physical service address in Canada is maintained and a registered agent accepts service of process. For the ISIC 7420 stock-photo/AI marketplace, a virtual office is acceptable as the initial registered seat, but it does not by itself establish substantive Canadian tax residency or GST/HST nexus; the corporation should maintain real operational activity, contracts, and personnel in Canada to satisfy Canada Revenue Agency substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5–10% probability of unannounced on-site verification within the first three years for a low-risk digital stock-photo/AI commercial marketplace, absent tax arrears, foreign-entity misuse indicators, or FINTRAC reporting events.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 8-9 (incorporation), s. 16 (corporate name), s. 19 (registered office), s. 103 (directors), s. 106 (officers); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; shares may be issued for any consideration fixed by the directors. No escrow account is required unless the corporation becomes a reporting issuer under provincial securities law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Incorporation filed with Corporations Canada are hereby adopted and ratified. (2) The corporation shall issue 100 Common Shares to the incorporator for C$100 paid-in consideration; shares are fully subscribed. (3) The registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], [Province], and the address is approved as the corporation's statutory records office. (4) [Director Name] is appointed sole director for the current term. (5) The following officers are appointed: President — [Name]; Secretary — [Name]; Treasurer — [Name]. (6) The officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, onboard payment providers including Stripe and PayPal, and execute all operational documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada / NUANS system via accredited federal name-search firms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through an accredited NUANS search house; verify the proposed name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing registered entities or trademarks; reserve the approved name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Requested corporate name in English and/or French
Detailed description of business activities (stock-photo/AI visual content services)
NUANS search request form and service fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised NUANS search or proceed as a numbered corporation (e.g., 1234567 Canada Inc.) without further name approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation with Corporations Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) and Form 4002 (Initial Registered Office and First Board of Directors); declare an unlimited share structure of Common shares without par value; designate the province of the registered office; submit digitally and pay the filing fee; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form 4001 – Articles of Incorporation
Form 4002 – Initial Registered Office and First Board of Directors
NUANS name search report (unless a numbered corporation is used)
Director's written consent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Notice of Defective Filing is received, correct the deficiencies within the statutory curable period (generally 60 days) and resubmit; no re-filing fee applies if corrected within the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply electronically for the 9-digit Business Number (BN); register for GST/HST once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per trailing four quarters (voluntary registration permitted for early input tax credits); register for payroll deductions if employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Director/officer personal identification and contact details
Registered office address
Estimated annual taxable revenue in Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA verification letters are resolved through My Business Account or the Business Window (1-800-959-5525); retroactive tax account amendments can be made under the Excise Tax Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Governance and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting; pass the First Board Resolution; adopt By-law No. 1 granting officers full operational authority; prepare the minute book with register of directors, register of shareholders, and share certificates; file the annual return with Corporations Canada within 60 days of each anniversary.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution
By-law No. 1 (general governance)
Share certificate ledger and transfer register
Minute book (physical or digital corporate records database)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in governance records are cured by supplemental board resolution without governmental filing; all records must remain consistent with filings on file with Corporations Canada.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration and Municipal Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial service registry (e.g., ServiceOntario) and municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation opens a physical office in a province, register as an extra-provincial corporation with the provincial registrar within 30 days of establishing a place of business; apply for a municipal general business licence and occupancy permit for the office premises; for a purely online stock-photo operation, a registered virtual office or mail-forwarding service may satisfy the provincial presence requirement.
required_dossiers: Federal Certificate of Incorporation
Certified extracts of Form 4001 / Form 4002
Provincial extra-provincial licence application
Municipal occupancy permit or home-based business certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provincial registry rejections are cured by amending the application or submitting certified English/French translations; municipal zoning refusals require leasing compliant premises or relocating the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Configure Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or credit union; payment processors (Stripe/PayPal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present corporate records and the signed resolution at a Canadian financial institution; complete KYC and beneficial-ownership attestation; verify Stripe Canada and PayPal Merchant accounts using the CRA BN; no statutory licence is required under Canadian payment-card network rules for this low-risk digital media revenue stream.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Minute book / register of directors and shareholders
First Board Resolution appointing signing officers
CRA BN confirmation letter
Directors' government-issued photo identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank triggers enhanced due diligence, provide a source-of-funds declaration and updated corporate profile; escalate to the branch manager or select an alternative Schedule I bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7420 stock-photo/AI visual-asset platform is a non-manufacturing digital service; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) exercises only general digital-economy oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None federally; optional municipal general business licence may apply depending on the city of the registered office (e.g., City of Toronto Municipal Code Ch. 545).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is office-based data processing with no physical facility triggering the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 1, Schedule 1.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point-source discharge; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be recycled under provincial e-waste regulations (e.g., Ontario O. Reg. 393/04); general office HVAC and water use must comply with municipal by-laws and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 for low-risk commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and occupancy-load clearance under the applicable provincial Fire Code (e.g., Ontario O. Reg. 213/07); electrical safety certification of office workspace; occupational health and safety program registration with the provincial workers' compensation board (e.g., WSIB in Ontario); the Canada Labour Code, Part II applies only if the corporation employs federally regulated employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/business-registration) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/my-business-account). In Quebec, Revenu Quebec additionally administers the QST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) before carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada. Procedure: (1) complete Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) or register online via Business Registration Online (BRO); (2) provide entity formation documents (federal/provincial articles of incorporation, certificate of status), registered office address, Canadian permanent establishment address, and a Canadian agent/representative for service of process; (3) select the 'RT' GST/HST program account suffix; (4) when the GST/HST account is opened, begin charging GST/HST on taxable supplies made in Canada on the effective date; (5) retain the CRA-issued confirmation letter and quote the BN on all invoices. A non-resident that only makes export supplies (zero-rated) may elect to register voluntarily to claim input tax credits; mandatory registration applies once the CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Canadian 'Business Corporation' (federal/provincial, elf 8615) is a resident corporation subject to Part I Income Tax Act on worldwide income at entity level; no pass-through, no check-the-box, and no elective transparent treatment for domestic corporations. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit relief; active business income earned through a controlled foreign affiliate is deferred until repatriation under the exempt surplus regime, while foreign accrual property income (FAPI) is taxed currently. A Canadian corporation cannot elect into partnership or disregarded-entity status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Canada; hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 ITA) apply automatically. Statutory elections available: (1) s. 89(11) ITA election to be deemed not to be a Canadian-controlled private corporation; (2) s. 85(1) ITA rollover election for tax-deferred transfer of property to the corporation; (3) s. 156 Excise Tax Act election between closely related corporations (90% common share value/votes) to deem intercorporate supplies to be made for nil consideration for GST/HST; (4) s. 150(3) Excise Tax Act election for a person with de minimis financial services revenue to be deemed not to be a financial institution; (5) for foreign corporations with a Canadian permanent establishment, the Part XIV branch tax can be reduced by an applicable income tax treaty without election, except that treaty-based waivers are claimed via CRA Form NR301/NR302 in respect of withholding.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; federal GST is 5%, and in HST provinces the combined federal-provincial HST applies (Ontario 13%; Nova Scotia 15%; New Brunswick 15%; Newfoundland and Labrador 15%; Prince Edward Island 15%), while the remaining provinces and territories apply 5% GST with separate provincial sales tax (PST) or GST-only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the 'small supplier' threshold is exceeded if the supplier (including associated corporations) makes worldwide taxable supplies of more than CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter, or more than CAD 30,000 in aggregate in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory. A non-resident is deemed to be carrying on business in Canada if it solicits orders in Canada (in person or through an agent) or maintains an inventory in Canada; non-resident suppliers of digital services and online marketplace operators are also subject to mandatory registration under the specified digital services rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), pre-clearance approval, API-reporting mandate, or digital stamping requirement exists under the Excise Tax Act. The CRA accepts paper and electronic invoices (PDF, EDI, XML, PEPPOL) if they contain the supplier's name, GST/HST registration number, date, recipient identification, description of supply, tax rate, and tax amount. E-invoices must be retained in an intelligible format for six years, and records located outside Canada must be made electronically available to the CRA on request; there is no advance digital clearance or fiscal invoice numbering regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act: (1) s. 7 zero-rates a service supplied to a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST and is not carrying on business in Canada, where the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada and not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time it is performed, and is not for use in Canada by the non-resident; (2) s. 10 zero-rates a supply of intangible personal property (including copyrights, digital licences, stock-photo/image licences, and generative visual asset rights) made to a non-resident non-registered person, unless the property is for use in Canada by the recipient otherwise than exclusively in the course of commercial activities; (3) exports of tangible goods are zero-rated when the supplier ships the goods to a destination outside Canada. For a Stock Photography Marketplace / Generative Visual Assets platform (ISIC 7420 / NAICS 541922), licence fees charged to non-resident licensees are zero-rated where the asset is downloaded or used outside Canada, or used in Canada exclusively in the licensee's commercial activities; supplies to Canadian-resident customers and to non-residents carrying on business in Canada are taxable at 5% GST/13-15% HST. The zero-rating claim is substantiated by evidence of the recipient's non-resident status (e.g., residential/business address, foreign registration records), the contractual place-of-use clause, and geo-IP or digital delivery logs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For physical goods exports: Canadian Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A / electronic export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System), Commercial Invoice, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, Packing List

For services/IP exports: fully executed licence or subscription agreement identifying the non-resident licensee (legal name, jurisdiction, registered address), asset description, permitted-use scope, and territorial exclusivity clause
GST/HST zero-rated invoice issued with 0% rate, citing the applicable zero-rating provision (s. 7 or s. 10, Part V, Schedule VI) and the licensee's non-resident status
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or acquiring-bank foreign-currency payment confirmation evidencing receipt of the licence fee from outside Canada within 180 days of invoicing

Supporting operational records: geo-IP download logs, digital delivery receipts, user KYC/onboarding data, IP registration records, and commission statements proving the offshore destination of the digital asset
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST within the four-year normal reassessment period (extended indefinitely for misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud). If a zero-rating claim fails on audit, the supplier is assessed 5% GST/13-15% HST on the full licence fee with compound interest, and any input tax credits relying on the zero-rated export stream are clawed back. Civil penalties: failure to file/remit penalty (s. 280 Excise Tax Act), gross-negligence penalty equal to 25% of the understated net tax (s. 285), and a 10% penalty for large cross-border transfer-pricing misstatements (s. 247(8) Income Tax Act) where the adjustment exceeds CAD 5,000. Criminal sanctions (s. 327 Excise Tax Act) for wilful evasion carry fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; fabricated bills of lading, depository receipts, or shell non-resident licensees trigger joint CRA-CBSA enforcement referrals, and directors/officers face personal liability for unremitted amounts under s. 323 Excise Tax Act. CRA also verifies that inward remittances in foreign currency are genuine, arm's length, and economically associated with the purported export; invoices outstanding beyond 180 days are rebuttably presumed not to support the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange and monetary policy conduct governed by the Bank of Canada Act, with banking supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and AML/ATF administration by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free-floating currency with full current-account and capital-account convertibility. No prior-exchange-control approval is required for foreign investment, dividend remittance, interest payments, or profit repatriation; the only constraints are the Investment Canada Act net-benefit review for controlling acquisitions above statutory thresholds, Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, often reduced by treaty), and corporate law solvency tests for dividends. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for all business purposes and there are no exchange control permits restricting commercial payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion obligation exists for export proceeds or digital-service receipts. Export earnings may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency without Bank of Canada authorization; reporting is limited to FINTRAC cross-border currency and monetary instrument reports for physical movements above CAD 10,000, plus routine income tax and GST/HST declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, conditional on registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with the Bank of Canada and FINTRAC designation as a foreign money services business. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer may be used only as settlement gateways for low-value royalty disbursements and must not hold corporate operating funds on a commingled basis; unlicensed foreign EMIs are prohibited from providing retail payment services to Canadians after the RPAA transitional period, and all capital and tax balances must remain dual-custody separated with a Tier 1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier 1 Canadian banks in practice require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner of the U.S. parent to attend an in-person branch interview for first-time corporate onboarding, or to complete a dual-step remote video identity verification with a notarized corporate certificate and apostilled registry extracts; fully remote onboarding without any physical or biometric step is generally unavailable for non-resident-owned private corporations. FINTRAC guidance permits client identification through affiliate or agent methods, and a Canadian legal opinion on beneficial ownership materially reduces onboarding friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership (U.S. parent) with no Canadian-resident director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organization chart; certificate of corporate status for the U.S. parent; beneficial ownership registry extract under the Canada Business Corporations Act transparency register; board resolution appointing the Canadian director; source-of-funds statement backed by 12 months of U.S. bank statements; notarized identification for all 25% or greater beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented high-volume micro-royalty revenue from global stock photography marketplaces and generative AI licensing via PayPal, Stripe, and agency remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed license and distribution agreements; monthly marketplace settlement reports; invoicing and royalty reconciliation ledgers; audited trial balance; transactional profiling letter to the bank; documented AML controls over payment aggregators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and jurisdiction exposure from open marketplace downloads by traffic geolocated to OFAC or Canadian sanctioned countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP geolocation block logs; terms-of-service prohibition of sanctioned users; sanctions screening policy covering OFAC SDN, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act listings, and the Canadian Financial Sanctions list; FINTRAC suspicious transaction report escalation protocol; enterprise-wide sanctions risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or PEP flags on directors or beneficial owners, and potential historical cryptocurrency receipt exposure from AI asset sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent background screening reports from World-Check or Dow Jones; PEP questionnaire and source-of-wealth narrative; declaration that no crypto-denominated proceeds are accepted; audit trail confirming that all settlement proceeds convert to fiat only at regulated exchanges; compliance attestation by the designated AML officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The U.S. parent shall inject initial capital by SWIFT MT103 from a U.S. bank to the RBC Capital Escrow Account with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' (narrative 'Subscription for common shares'); funds may arrive in USD and be converted to CAD on the spot market at the bank's prevailing rate, or held in a segregated USD account until drawdown. The verification pack includes an executed board resolution, amended articles if applicable, FATCA/CRS self-certification, and source-of-funds confirmation; no Bank of Canada approval is required given Canada's full capital-account convertibility.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty disbursements to international contributors will be settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 via the Tier 1 bank's cross-border payments API for transactions above CAD 10,000 equivalent, and through SEPA or Automated Clearing House batches for EU, UK, and U.S. contributors; commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for digital royalty flows and would be used only for ancillary physical merchandise sales. All outbound disbursements are subject to FINTRAC threshold monitoring, OFAC/SEMA sanctions screening, and bank-required transaction narrative codes for 'Royalty Payment' or 'License Fee'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Tier 1 bank dealing room, maturities up to 24 months
CAD/USD European-style plain vanilla FX options, purchased or collared
Cross-currency swaps (USD floating versus CAD floating) to neutralize balance-sheet translation risk on USD revenue accounts

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted only for third-currency exposure in thinly traded emerging market currencies; CAD/USD NDFs are legally permissible but uneconomic given the deep deliverable market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return filed with Corporations Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the deadline is based on the anniversary date of incorporation, not the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated non-filing triggers a notice of default and administrative dissolution risk under CBCA s. 212; reinstatement costs and arrears apply once dissolved; directors may face personal liability for corporate debts and taxes incurred during the default period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and related CRA annual filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, with an additional 10% penalty for repeat failures within 3 years; daily compound arrears interest; directors may be liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under CBCA s. 163, a non-distributing corporation is exempt from appointing an auditor if its gross revenues in the most recent fiscal year do not exceed CAD 1,000,000 and the shareholders waive the audit appointment; distributing (public) corporations and corporations exceeding this threshold must appoint a licensed public accountant as auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS as adopted in Canada; private enterprises may apply IFRS or Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); tax reporting requires a reconciliation from accounting income to taxable income under the Income Tax Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate federal UBO annual return filing is currently required for a non-distributing CBCA corporation; however, the corporation must maintain a current Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) under CBCA s. 21.1 and update it within 15 days after becoming aware of any change, including share transfers or changes in control; the ISC register must be retained with other corporate records and disclosed to the Director of Corporations Canada upon request

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general corporate rate; combined federal-provincial headline rate of approximately 23%-27% where the corporation maintains a permanent establishment in a province (provincial rates range from 8% in Alberta to 12% in Quebec and the Maritime provinces).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on the first C$500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations; SR&ED Investment Tax Credit: up to 35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs on AI image-generation and software R&D; 100% Class 12 CCA for computer software and 55% Class 50 CCA for data-processing/server hardware; full s.112 deduction for intercorporate dividends; non-capital loss carryback of 3 years and carryforward of 20 years; net capital losses carryback 3 years and carryforward indefinitely.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via CRA EFILE or Internet Transfer using CRA-certified tax preparation software; electronic filing is mandatory for corporations with gross revenues exceeding C$1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due 6 months after fiscal year-end; Part I balance due 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs); T106 transfer-pricing information return due 6 months after year-end; NR4 withholding slips due by March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales of goods and services: stock photo licensing fees, subscription revenue, generative AI visual asset sales, and marketplace commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only gross revenue attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment; direct cross-border licensing revenue for non-resident sellers may be Part XIII royalty income rather than business income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income after deduction of cost of goods sold, commission fees to Stripe/PayPal, cloud hosting, contributor payouts, AI training data licenses, and advertising costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions allowed only to the extent they are reasonable and incurred to earn Canadian-source business income; transfer-pricing adjustments apply for cross-border related-party cost allocations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income under s.3(a); includes business income, property income, taxable capital gains on IP sales, and foreign investment income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations include only Canadian-source income; foreign-source business income may be excluded unless a s.115 determination applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deductions; taxable income after loss carryovers, capital cost allowance adjustments, and reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty non-discrimination provisions where computing taxable income of a Canadian PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I federal tax on taxable income at 15% after the provincial abatement; Schedule 1 computes the federal and provincial allocation using gross revenue and payroll factors for PE provinces
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations file Schedule 1 to allocate taxable income among provinces based on permanent establishment gross revenue and salary/wage factors

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax before non-refundable credits and total refundable/non-refundable tax payable; general corporate tax credits claimed on Schedules 51 (SR&ED ITC) and 23, 24
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim SR&ED only for expenditures attributable to Canadian PE activities; provincial credits require provincial PE presence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital Cost Allowance schedule: Class 12 (100%) for software, Class 50 (55% declining balance) for computer hardware, Class 39/40 for plant and equipment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCA is available only where the depreciable asset is used for earning income in Canada; accelerated CCA must be prorated where foreign-source income is excluded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Arm's-Length Transactions schedule cross-referencing T106 filings for transactions with related non-resident entities; mandatory when aggregate FMV exceeds C$1M
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intercompany royalty, commission, cloud-service, and contributor-payout arrangements with non-resident affiliates; provide arm's-length pricing justification

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s.162(2): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeat offenders incur a 10% base penalty plus 2% per month up to 20 months; no-balance-owing late returns incur a minimum C$100 penalty; failure to file T106 attracts C$100 per month per unreported property or service up to C$2,500; daily compounded interest accrues at the prescribed rate (90-day T-bill rate plus 4% per annum) on all unpaid amounts from the original due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; treaty-reduced to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the payer's voting shares and 15% for portfolio shareholders (Canada-US DTA and most OECD-based Canada tax treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Canadian payer must (i) obtain a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial-ownership declaration from the non-resident shareholder (CRA Form NR301 for US residents, NR74 or W-8BEN-E equivalent for other treaty jurisdictions); (ii) withhold the DTA-reduced rate at source and remit Part XIII amounts by the 15th day of the month following payment; (iii) file NR4 Summary and Information Returns by March 31; (iv) if tax was over-withheld, non-resident files Form NR7-R with TRC supporting a refund claim within the two-year limitation under s.227(6); treaty relief is denied where the non-resident lacks economic substance in its home jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, software, copyrights, and AI visual assets: statutory 25% under s.212(1)(d); Canada-US DTA exempts to 0% royalties on computer software, copyrights, and patents paid by a Canadian payer to a related US resident, with other royalties capped at 10%; interest: statutory 25% under s.212(1)(b); treaty rate reduced to 0% for arm's-length interest under Canada-US and most comprehensive DTAs, with non-arm's-length interest remaining fully taxable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1M aggregate fair-market value of all non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents triggers mandatory CRA Form T106; CRA expects contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation when total cross-border intercompany transactions exceed C$5M; Country-by-Country Report (Form RC7000) mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding C$1B.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations registration exists in Canada; substance is tested through (i) central management and control residence analysis; (ii) the 'carrying on business in Canada' permanent establishment rubric under s.253 and s.255.1; (iii) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in s.245; (iv) transfer-pricing documentation obligations; (v) thin-capitalization limits in s.18(4)-(5) and the new Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses (EIFR) 30% EBITDA cap for years beginning after October 1, 2023; a stock-photo AI platform holding only IP licenses and payment-gateway contracts with no Canadian premises, employees, or management will be considered substance-less and exposed to income re-attribution and Part XIII withholding assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating gross photo-licensing and AI-asset revenue on the T2 (undisclosed Stripe and PayPal settlements), fabricating contributor-payout and AI-training-data expenses, or destroying financial records during a CRA audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163.2: 50% of the understated federal and provincial tax; criminal conviction under s.239 on indictment: fine of 100% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment up to 5 years; Criminal Code fraud s.380 carries up to 14 years where the fraud exceeds C$1M; CRA may seize assets via s.160/non-arm's-length assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized false filings are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts under s.227.1 with no relief where gross negligence is proven; CRA can freeze personal bank accounts, issue director travel bans under s.225.2-225.6, and pursue criminal fraud charges with personal restitution obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a 'headless' Canadian business corporation with nominee directors, no physical premises, and no employees; inserting the shell between a non-resident AI stock-photo owner and Canadian payment rails to avoid Canadian-source business income classification; using a conduit that has no central management in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR adjustment under s.245 re-attributing licensing revenue to the non-resident beneficial owner; GAAR penalty of 25% of the tax benefit plus arrears interest; deemed-PE assessment under s.253; foreign-reporting penalties up to C$2,500 per unreported Form T1135 plus C$25 per day for each late form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face false-declaration penalties under s.163.2 (minimum C$100 up to 50% of the tax attributable to the misrepresentation); participation in the shell scheme can ground Criminal Code fraud charges and civil fraudulent-conveyance claims against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying supra-normal royalties or technical service fees to a related non-resident licensor with no substantive personnel; funding the AI photo platform through non-resident shareholder debt exceeding the 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio; failing to file T106 for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in excess of C$1M; using unverifiable CUP pricing for generative asset transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA re-determination of profits under s.247(2) on arm's-length terms; documentation penalty of C$1,000 per month up to C$24,000; s.247(3)(b) penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where reasonable documentation is absent; denial of interest deductions under thin-cap rules; EIFR limitation of net interest to 30% of tax-adjusted EBITDA; daily compounded interest on all reassessed amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed inaccurate T106 filings or declarations are subject to gross-negligence penalties under s.163.2; directors who orchestrated the conduit-pricing structure may be personally assessed as participants in the tax benefit, with personal restitution liability and possible international travel prohibitions pending CRA criminal referral.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and MSB Payment Rail Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Stripe and PayPal settlement flows through nominee or third-country bank accounts to conceal ultimate beneficial ownership; failure to register as a money services business; failure to perform KYB/KYC on high-volume stock-photo contributors; processing payments for non-verified or 'ghost' contributor accounts; deliberate layering of AI asset licensing revenue through multiple jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under PCMLTFA up to C$1,000,000 per violation for corporations and C$500,000 for individuals; failure-to-register is a criminal offense punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment; criminal money laundering under s.462.31 Criminal Code carries up to 10 years imprisonment; forfeiture of funds under s.462.38; FINTRAC suspends MSB tolerances where suspicious-transaction reporting fails on Stripe/PayPal payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who directed, authorized, or acquiesced in AML violations are personally liable under s.73.1 PCMLTFA with fines up to C$500,000; directors may be prosecuted for money laundering as principals; travel bans can be imposed to prevent flight pending resolution of the AML and tax charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident shareholders, licensors, or lenders at a treaty-reduced or zero rate without obtaining a valid TRC or NR301 declaration; reclassifying taxable Canadian-source royalty income as cost reimbursement or intercompany loan principal to avoid Part XIII withholding; remitting amounts late or on an erroneous basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Aggravated non-remittance penalty of 10% of the amount under s.227(9); late remittance penalty of 3% per month up to 12 months on a repeat basis; NR4 filing penalty of C$25 per day per slip up to C$2,500; s.212.2 re-characterization of disguised distributions as dividends subject to Part XIII; interest compounding daily from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors have strict joint-and-several personal liability for unremitted Part XIII withholdings under s.227.1; the deemed-trust amount is not dischargeable in personal bankruptcy; CRA may collect from personal assets of directors within 2 years of the corporate dissolution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling shares of the profitable AI stock-photo operating company to a non-resident purchaser while converting accumulated retained earnings into an ostensible capital gain instead of a taxable dividend; using post-sale forced surplus distributions to circumvent the 25% dividend withholding tax; structuring redemption transactions to trigger s.84(2) deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.84.1 re-characterizes share sale proceeds as a dividend requiring Part XIII withholding at 25%; s.246 imposes tax on artificial surplus-stripping arrangements; CRA applies GAAR to eliminate the tax benefit; interest under s.161(1) runs from the original dividend date; s.212.2 deems a dividend where winding-up distributions avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who implemented the strip can be reassessed as principal shareholders and become personally liable for unpaid withholding tax arising from the deeming provisions; misrepresentation of fair value in the share sale exposes directors to s.163.2 penalties and criminal fraud liability.
